name: USS Clemson
shortDescription: Nimble early torpedo boat that lives and dies by concealment.

torpedoMounts.note: All four mounts traverse a full 180°, none are locked to one side.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: 5s action, 40s cooldown, one of the fastest resets you'll see at this tier.

consumables.name: Smoke Generator
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 30s to lay, roughly 112s screen off a 160s cooldown. Built to park a team inside, not to dash through.

strengths: Excellent concealment for the tier, usually gets the first spot
Twelve torpedo tubes across four mounts, an enormous alpha strike for tier III
Small and nimble enough to dodge return fire
weaknesses: No real armor, a couple of cruiser salvos will end you
Gun DPM is weak next to other tier III destroyers
Short torpedo range forces you in close
tips: Don't start a gunfight on purpose. Your guns finish off a low-health target, they don't win fights.
Use your concealment to spot enemy destroyers first, then decide whether to back off or commit.
Save the smoke for breaking contact. It's too valuable this early to burn on damage farming alone.

threats.reason: One HE salvo can end you, and their guns outrange yours.
If they spot you first, the fight is already lost.

summary: Smallest, hardest-to-spot destroyer at her tier.
A torpedo boat first, guns are strictly a last resort.
Paper-thin. One good salvo ends the game.
playstyle.detail: Clemson isn't built to win a fight in the open. She's built to avoid being in one. Stay hidden, line up the angle, and let the torpedoes make your case for you. The instant someone spots you back, the plan has already gone sideways, so don't wait around to find out how badly.

imageCredit: USS Clemson (DD-186) steaming at high speed, c. 1919. Naval History and Heritage Command, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

goalTags.note: One of the lowest detection ranges you'll find this early. Built to stay unseen.
Four triple mounts, twelve tubes total. Very few ships this early can put that much ordnance in the water at once.
